The Events of Yakuza

October, 1995. Kamurocho, one of Asia's largest entertainment districts.
In this town swirling with desire and violence lived a yakuza by the
name of Kazuma Kiryu, a Lieutenant Advisor of the prestigious Dojima Family.

But he was better known as "The Dragon of Dojima."

He was a rising star, and soon he would take control over a family
of his own...

The Events of Yakuza

At Kiryu's side was his best friend, Akira Nishikiyama.
The two grew up together in Sunflower Orphanage and swore
their oaths to the Tojo Clan's Dojima Family on the same day.

The pair was often joined by Yumi Sawamura, another of
Sunflower's orphans, whom they treated like a younger sister.

The happy days where the three of them would get together and drink
at the upscale bar, Serena, are some of Kiryu's fondest memories...

But one stormy night, their lives changed forever.

The Events of Yakuza

The Patriarch of the Dojima Family, Sohei Dojima, kidnapped Yumi,
prompting Nishikiyama to shoot him in a blind frenzy.

Kiryu arrived at the scene to find Nishikiyama still holding the
smoking gun, and Kiryu made a fateful decision: In order to ensure
Nishikiyama could still be around for his ill sister, Kiryu took
the gun in hand and sent both Nishikiyama and Yumi out of the building. 
 
That day, Kiryu became a patriarch killer, a crime above all crimes
in the criminal world of the yakuza.

Kiryu was jailed and expelled from the organization, and Yumi,
suffering from traumatic memory loss, disappeared from the hospital.

The Events of Yakuza

Ten years passed...
December, 2005. Kiryu emerges from prison to a changed world.

Nishikiyama had lost his sister and suffered greatly in the
ten years, and as a result, had twisted into a monster,
obsessed with power and climbing the ranks of the Tojo Clan.

Not even Shintaro Kazama, Patriarch of the Kazama Family and
founder of Sunflower Orphanage, a father figure to them both,
could stay Nishikiyama's dark transformation.

The Events of Yakuza

In a meeting of the Tojo Clan's direct patriarchs, Nishikiyama,
now patriarch of his own family, exposed the fact that ten billion
yen had been stolen from the clan's coffers.

In the ensuing chaos, the Tojo Clan's third chairman, Masaru Sera,
was murdered, and an assassination attempt was made on Kazama right
before Kiryu's eyes.

And as the Tojo Clan crumbled, Goro Majima, the Mad Dog of Shimano,
began to play in the ashes.

The conflict nearly escalated into a civil war, and the shadow of
the Nishikiyama Family loomed large over the incident...

The Events of Yakuza

As Kiryu became embroiled in the Tojo Clan's internal conflict, he
continued his search for Yumi, who was still missing after all these years.

Seeking clues at Serena, he learned that Yumi had a younger sister
by the name of Mizuki. Believing Mizuki to be his only lead, Kiryu plunged
into the darkness of the city to find her.

But Mizuki's trail was no warmer than Yumi's, and as all hope began to
fade, Kiryu finally caught his break<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>he encountered a young girl who
claimed to be the daughter of Mizuki.

The Events of Yakuza

The girl's name was Haruka Sawamura.

Despite being only nine years old, she came to Kamurocho herself in
hopes of finding her mother, Mizuki. Like Kiryu, Haruka too had grown
up in Sunflower Orphanage, and her Aunt Yumi had entrusted her
with a pendant said to be "worth ten billion yen."

The criminal underworld was drawn to the girl and the pendant like moths
to a flame. Kamurocho became engulfed in conspiracy and betrayal,
with Nishikiyama at the heart of the conflict.

The Events of Yakuza

Kiryu and Haruka finally caught up to Kazama, who was able to explain
the whole truth of the incident.

Haruka was in fact, Yumi's daughter. Mizuki was simply Yumi's alias,
created to protect her from a politician by the name of Kyohei Jingu.

Not only did the Tojo Clan's missing funds actually belong to Jingu,
but he was also Haruka's father. Jingu had manipulated the Tojo Clan from
the shadows in an effort to dispose of his scandalously illegitimate daughter.

In an effort to chip away at his power, Kazama, Yumi, and Sera had teamed up
to steal his ten billion yen.

The Events of Yakuza

To reclaim his money, Jingu singled out Nishikiyama's ambition to become
the successor to the late Sera and used that as a means to an end. The
two both stood to gain, as Nishikiyama would become the fouth chairman.

However, the Tojo Clan's true successor was written in the secret will
of Sera, with Kazama as its witness: None other than Kazuma Kiryu. 

Declaring this to Jingu, Kiryu crushed him and his entire special
forces unit, and then settled the score with Nishikiyama.

The Events of Yakuza

An explosion rocked the Millennium Tower where the money had been held.
As money fluttered into the streets, the people who Kiryu cared about more
than anyone in the world breathed their last.

Yumi, who shielded Kiryu from a bullet fired by Jingu.

Nishikiyama, who in his final moments smiled at Kiryu as he ignited
the bomb to take accountability for his actions and end the bloodshed...

The Events of Yakuza

In that moment of despair, Kiryu lost his will to go on. But there in
front of him was Haruka, now the only living legacy of Yumi, the woman
he'd come to love.

Kiryu took Haruka's hand. The Dragon of Dojima and the "Girl Worth
Ten Billion Yen" took their first steps together...

The Events of Yakuza 2

December, 2006. Kazuma Kiryu became the legendary yakuza who had
ascended to the Tojo Clan's fourth chairman and retired the same day.

But in the wake of the ten billion yen incident, the Tojo Clan weakened,
having lost its most prominent leaders in the turmoil.

The eye of the Omi Alliance, western Japan's largest yakuza organization,
turned east. To avoid an all-out war, the Tojo Clan's fifth chairman,
Yukio Terada, told Kiryu of a plan to broker peace with the Omi.

However...

The Events of Yakuza 2

The Omi Alliance made the first move, assassinating Yukio Terada
and turning all-out war between the two factions into a fearsome reality.

Without a chairman to lead them, Kiryu took Terada's place at the
negotiation table, dragging an unlikely candidate back into the fold
should things turn for the worse<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Daigo Dojima.

Daigo was the son of Sohei Dojima, and the mark of patricide still
hung over Kiryu for his murder.

The Events of Yakuza 2

The night before the meeting with the Omi Alliance was to take
place in Sotenbori, Osaka, Kiryu met a new foe<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>the Dragon of Kansai,
Ryuji Goda. Goda was Patriarch of the Go-Ryu Clan, and none other than
the son of Jin Goda, the fifth chairman of the Omi Alliance.

"There's only room for one dragon in this world."

Boasting of "grand fireworks" about to be set off, as if on cue,
the Kazama Family office in Kamurocho went up in flames.

The Events of Yakuza 2

Ryuji ignited his coup with his own father as the kindling.
As negotiations between Kiryu and Goda began, Ryuji's Go-Ryu Clan
infiltrated the proceedings, laying bare his desire to conquer
the world of the yakuza.

Forced into cooperation with the police, Kiryu began working alongside
Kaoru Sayama from the Osaka PD's 4th Division to stop Ryuji Goda. Through
this alliance, it became apparent that a tragedy that occurred over 20 years
ago in Kamurocho was connected to them both.

The Events of Yakuza 2

The Jingweon Mafia, a Korean mainland crime syndicate, was all but
wiped out in a raid organized by Sohei Dojima in the early 1980s.

Under Dojima's orders, it was none other than Shintaro Kazama, the
man who raised Kiryu, who led the raid.

But there were survivors, including a very young Ryuji Goda...

The survivors of the massacre desired nothing but revenge, and over
20 years later, the opportunity arose in the chance to envelop the
Tojo Clan in an all-out east-versus-west war.

The Events of Yakuza 2

One of the massacre's survivors was in fact Yukio Terada, who had
staged his death in order to set the plot in motion. But to Terada,
revenge was both his destiny and his burden...

As the events of the massacre came to light, Kaoru Sayama discovered
that she was actually the half-sister of Ryuji Goda. But as the bonds
of blood thickened, so too, did it spill. Kiryu stood in the center
of the pool, seeking to end the cycle of hatred and revenge.

The Events of Yakuza 2

It was only Ryuji Goda who fought not for blood, but for pride.
He wanted nothing more than to surpass the legendary yakuza and
become the sole surviving dragon.

"There's only room for one dragon in this world."
 
With the schemers and conspirators of the Jingweon plot bleeding out
of the picture, Kiryu and Ryuji prepared for a showdown.

The Events of Yakuza 2

The two dragons roared as they threw themselves into an all-out battle
for supremacy.

It was Ryuji who finally fell.

The war of east versus west fell silent as the conflict between two
dragons decided its fate...

The Events of Yakuza 3

2009, Ryukyugai, Okinawa<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>a southern tropical island practically a
world removed from the daily grind of Kamurocho.
 
Kiryu and Haruka returned to their roots, becoming the proprietors of
Morning Glory orphanage, living amongst a small group of children with no
relatives.

But not even this remote beach was safe from the yakuza. Only a year
ago, the Ryudo Family had served them an eviction notice in an effort
to clear the land for the building of a luxury resort along the coast.

The Events of Yakuza 3

Shigeru Nakahara, Patriarch of the Ryudo Family, believed the resort
was the key to a future of prosperity for Okinawa, despite his love
for the quiet serenity that such a resort would destroy.

Kiryu's resolve to protect the home of these children showed Nakahara
what would be lost in the process, and a friendship was forged.

But not more than a year later... Nakahara was shot.

The Events of Yakuza 3

Kiryu could not contain his rage. Nakahara's adoptive daughter, who saw
the culprit, drew his face... and Kiryu could not believe his eyes.
It was the spitting image of Kazama, his father figure who had died
in his arms.

Not longer after, news of another shooting reached Kiryu. Daigo Dojima,
whom Kiryu had entrusted the future of the Tojo Clan to, was also shot
by the mysterious assassin resembling Kazama.

The Events of Yakuza 3

An attack on the sixth chairman was enough to stir the Tojo Clan's newly
risen officers to action.

Yoshitaka Mine, Patriarch of the Hakuho Clan.
Tsuyoshi Kanda, Third Patriarch of the Nishikiyama Family.
Goh Hamazaki, Patriarch of the Hamazaki Family. 

With Daigo out of the picture, all of them began to play their hands,
and the ensuing clash pulled Kiryu and his new friends into the fold.

Kiryu was forced to return to Kamurocho to discover the truth: a foreign
arms dealing organization had lit the spark of the conflict.

The Events of Yakuza 3

"Black Monday" was its name, and at its head, a man named
Andre Richardson... 

Ryuzo Tamiya, the Japanese Minister of Defense, had allied with the
American CIA to lure out Black Monday. He'd leaked information about
the production of a ballistic missile system to lure Richardson to Japan...

And he took the bait. But the CIA also sent an agent to assist in his
capture... Joji Kazama, younger brother of Shintaro Kazama.

The Events of Yakuza 3

Tamiya revealed that the missile system and the resort development were
both, in truth, tactics deployed to bring Black Monday to the surface.

But the CIA had its own agenda, and Tamiya had no means of controlling
the streak of blood left in Joji Kazama's wake. To stop him, he turned to
Kiryu.

Meanwhile, back in Okinawa...

The Events of Yakuza 3

The Tojo Clan's struggle for dominance ended with Mine on top. He allied
with the Tamashiro Family of Ryukyugai, and Morning Glory orphanage could
not withstand their combined might. A surprise attack leveled the structure.

But Morning Glory was not the only casualty. Rikiya, the young captain
of the Ryudo Family was shot by Tamashiro and died in Kiryu's arms.

The attack on innocent lives was too much for Kiryu to take, and he
clenched his fists, preparing to take on Mine in earnest...

The Events of Yakuza 3

Mine had triumphed through his secret connection to Black Monday. He'd
joined the yakuza out of admiration for their life bonds that no amount
of money could sever.

But it was Daigo Dojima, who saw the true value in the humanity of his
subordinates, who became Mine's obsession. He rose through the ranks
of the Tojo Clan with Daigo as his impetus.

But with Daigo in critical condition after the gunshot wound, Mine entered
a downward spiral of despair.

The Events of Yakuza 3

Mine came to the conclusion that Daigo was in no condition to live as
he once had, and resolved to end his life to carry on the Tojo Clan's legacy.

Although Kiryu and Mine had both grown up as orphans, there could not
be a bigger gulf in their ideologies, and the two men clashed.

The battle came to an end with Black Monday's leader, Andre Richardson,
pointing his gun at Mine.

The Events of Yakuza 3

It was Daigo, arising from his comatose state, who saved Mine. But Mine,
seeing the error of his ways, chose to take accountability in his own way -
falling to his death with Richardson before Kiryu and Daigo's eyes.

As things settled down, Kiryu made ready to leave Kamurocho once more,
when a familiar face appeared in the crowd<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Goh Hamazaki, the disgraced
former Tojo Clan patriarch.

Blaming Kiryu and the Tojo for having lost everything, Kiryu offered a
hand of reconciliation... and Hamazaki responded by thrusting a knife into
Kiryu's ribs.

The Events of Yakuza 3

"Faced with death, you're capable of almost anything."

Those were the words Kiryu spoke to Hamazaki in the final moments,
and they were true of both Rikiya and Mine as well.

As he healed, Kiryu helped to piece Morning Glory back together,
brick by beam, looking out upon a peaceful horizon...

The Events of Yakuza 4

March 2010. A serial killer was loose in Kamurocho, and the tension
was both thick and volatile.

A loan shark by the name of Shun Akiyama rose to prominence as
the "Lifeline of Kamurocho" for loaning money to the type of people
a normal loan company would turn away at the door.

"Every jungle needs its lion."

Akiyama believed that with Kazuma Kiryu out of the picture, Kamurocho
had gone to the beasts.

The Events of Yakuza 4

One yakuza to earn Akiyama's respect was Hiroaki Arai, a captain of a
third-string Tojo Clan affiliate called Kanemura Enterprises.

But when a minor turf dispute erupted into a gun battle, Arai put a decisive
end to it and the rival Ueno Seiwa agitator before disappearing into the
night...

All it took was a bullet to shatter the fragile peace of the city. The
reconciliation efforts between the Tojo Clan's sixth chairman, Daigo Dojima,
and the Ueno Seiwa's captain, Isao Katsuragi deteriorated, with the honor
of both organizations on the line.

The Events of Yakuza 4

25 years ago, an incident occurred that neither the Tojo Clan nor the
Ueno Seiwa Clan could ever forget.

18 Ueno Seiwa yakuza were gunned down by Taiga Saejima, a young member
of the Tojo Clan's Sasai Family. Saejima was sentenced to death and
was still awaiting his execution from a prison cell in 2010.

The Events of Yakuza 4

As the events in Kamurocho began to unfold, Saejima was suddenly
transferred to a private correctional facility off the coast of
Okinawa called "Okinawa Penitentiary 2."

There, Saejima had a fateful encounter with none other than
Goh Hamazaki, former patriarch of the Tojo Clan's Hamazaki Family.

Hamazaki convinced Saejima of two things: One, that 25 years ago,
Saejima was betrayed by his sworn brother, Goro Majima... And two,
that in order to discover the truth, the two men would have to
break out of prison.

The Events of Yakuza 4

Masayoshi Tanimura was a police officer in the Community and Safety
Division of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department's Kamurocho Branch.
He came from a line of police officers, his own father having been
murdered in the line of duty 25 years ago.

The only lead to his father's killer was a name, scribbled in his father's
notebook<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Yasuko Saejima.

Yasuko, the younger sister of Taiga "18 Counts" Saejima was in Kamurocho
herself, and under the fake name of "Lily," had sought a loan of 100 million
yen from Akiyama's Sky Finance.

The Events of Yakuza 4

With acquittal for her brother dangled as bait, Yasuko was turned into a
serial killer<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>she was the one behind the murders in Kamurocho.

Three men became linked to the fate of this woman<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Taiga Saejima,
Shun Akiyama, and Masayoshi Tanimura.

In his escape from prison, Saejima ends up adrift at sea, washing up
on the beach of an orphanage... run by the Dragon of Dojima, Kazuma Kiryu.

The Events of Yakuza 4

Though their means are different, the four men eventually arrive at
the truth of the incident 25 years ago<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>

The Ueno Seiwa hit was an elaborate conspiracy, penned by Isao Katsuragi
himself in an effort to rise through the ranks of his clan.

Tanimura's father, who had discovered the truth, was murdered by one
of these conspirators<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Katsuragi's sworn brother.

But the conspiracy hadn't gone unnoticed in the police, and Seishiro
Munakata, deputy commissioner of the Tokyo Metropolitan police, had stepped
in to control the pieces on the board toward his own ends.

The Events of Yakuza 4

Munakata's corruption didn't end at the cover-up of the hit. The funding
for Okinawa Penitentiary 2 had also been Munakata's doing, and was
originally going to be secured from Kyohei Jingu in 2005. But that money
had gone up in smoke.

With his hands on both the police and the criminal underworld, Munakata
amassed so much power that neither the state nor Daigo Dojima, sixth chairman
of the Tojo Clan, could touch him.

The Events of Yakuza 4

At Munakata's behest, Daigo had Goro Majima arrested, who alongside the
four men tied to Yasuko, had become an obstacle.

The only ones left to carry on the fight were the outsiders of their
organizations<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>Kiryu, Tanimura, Saejima, and Akiyama.

The Events of Yakuza 4

Using Akiyama's vast wealth as bait, Munakata and his lackeys were drawn
out to the top of the Millennium Tower.

Saejima fought to avenge his sister, who had been shot by Katsuragi as
the conflict escalated.

Tanimura fought for justice, seeking to put an end to Munakata and the
cover-ups that obscured his father's killer.

Kiryu fought for honor. It was him that had put Daigo in the position of
sixth chairman, and it would be him who would set him back on the right path.

The Events of Yakuza 4

With his corruption coming to light and the utter failure of his plan,
Munakata took his own life.

With the conflict at an end, four men took new steps to forge a better
tomorrow...

The Events of Yakuza 5

December 2012. Daigo Dojima, sixth chairman of the Tojo Clan visited
Nagasugai, Fukuoka to arrange an alliance with the Yamagasa Family,
the most prominent family in the Kyushu region.

With rumors circulating that the seventh chairman of the Omi Alliance was on
his deathbed, it was imperative for Daigo to extend the hand of peace
to the yakuza organizations across Japan to mitigate the forthcoming
power struggle of the Omi Alliance.

But his visit served another purpose... To find Kazuma Kiryu, the legendary
yakuza who had disappeared...

The Events of Yakuza 5

Kiryu had returned to Morning Glory, but had been forced to distance
himself as Haruka Sawamura was scouted by an Osaka-based talent agency.

Kiryu, as connected to Haruka as he was, could not let his criminal past
come to light, or it would mean the death of Haruka's chances.

Kiryu took up life in Nagasugai as "Suzuki," a humble taxi driver. But
after a brief ride in his cab, Daigo Dojima disappeared, and the "Dragon of
Dojima" was once again thrust into the politics of the yakuza...

The Events of Yakuza 5

Meanwhile, Taiga Saejima, needing to clear his name of his previous crimes,
turned himself in, and was incarcerated in a prison called Abashiri.

While there, he was the target of constant attempts on his life, but it was
the news that Goro Majima, his sworn brother, had been killed that left
him no choice but to break out once again.

On the advice of Serizawa, an Osaka detective, Saejima headed for 
Kamurocho to learn the truth.

The Events of Yakuza 5

As the Tojo Clan began to stir, the Omi Alliance did as well, with two
captains in a dead heat for the succession to the Omi throne: Masaru Watase
and Naoki Katsuya.

The two men were ideological opposites. Watase was brash and ready for
war, while Katsuya was quiet and calculating, with immense control of the
entertainment industry in Osaka. But the apparent suicide of Mirei Park,
the woman who had scouted Haruka Sawamura, cast a shadow over his influence.

The Events of Yakuza 5

Haruka, who had been training for idol stardom under Park's watchful eyes,
was devastated by her death. That's when Shun Akiyama arrived in Osaka,
as he'd been the one to finance Park's talent agency. As the two worked to
discover the truth, they became entangled in the conflict of the yakuza...

The Events of Yakuza 5

In Nagoya, Daigo Dojima suddenly resurfaced. 

Daigo's high school classmate, a former professional baseball player
named Tatsuo Shinada, had been banned from the league after a gambling
scandal 15 years ago. Sensing a tie to the criminal underworld,
Daigo asks Shinada to dig up the truth of his own past.

Daigo had become aware that one yakuza mastermind was pulling the strings
behind the conflict in five cities...

The Events of Yakuza 5

As if by fate, the trail led to Kamurocho, and Kiryu, Saejima, Shinada,
Akiyama, and Haruka found themselves in the eye of the storm.

The mastermind of the plot Daigo had suspected finally revealed himself<symbol=em_dash_with_outline>
Tsubasa Kurosawa, seventh chairman of the Omi Alliance, who had been working
in the shadows as Serizawa, the Osaka police officer.

Kurosawa, who was dying of cancer, plotted to rid the world of "legendary"
yakuza like Kiryu so that the reins of power and everything he'd built could
be transferred successfully to his own son.

The Events of Yakuza 5

Kurosawa had planted his agents in every organization across the country,
and his schemes terrified even the most renowned yakuza.

As the conflict came to a head, Haruka began her first real concert at
the Japan Dome, and unbeknownst to her, became part of a plot to target
Kiryu with her assassination.

As his friends fell around him, Kiryu headed to the Tojo Clan headquarters,
where he found Masato Aizawa, Kurosawa's son.

The Events of Yakuza 5

Despite the lengths Kurosawa had gone to give Aizawa the world, Aizawa
saw no value in any of it, struggling to understand his own father's
motives for leaving him such a legacy.

But that doesn't stop him from accepting it. This father and son were
responsible for untold tragedies to countless people, and Kiryu accepted
the challenge of ending their power grab by becoming an insurmountable wall
for Aizawa.

The Events of Yakuza 5

Meanwhile... Haruka's concert sped toward its climax, as the throngs of
cheering people filled every inch of the dome. 

Haruka believed firmly that the dreams of an idol were not hers alone, but
those of everyone who had believed in her. A bright and shining future as
a popstar awaited her at the end of the forthcoming song...

At the cost of severing her ties to Kazuma Kiryu.

A path Haruka could not will herself to take.

The Events of Yakuza 5


"Kazuma Kiryu is family to me."

The crowd fell silent, stunned by Haruka's words. With all eyes on her,
Haruka ran from the stage she could now never return to.

Not far away, a soft snow fell gently into the pools of blood trailing
behind Kazuma Kiryu's bruised and beaten body. As his consciousness
faded, a dream came to him...

A dream of returning to his family...
